messages:
Marta (AE): Heads-up: ShadowGate wants a 4-day POC next Wed. Requirements: Private/VPC connectivity, perimeter TLS inspection (DPI), and a single allowlist egress IP for their firewall. They need a one-paragraph explanation for their security packet, a pasteable fw snippet, and a ballpark for POC pricing. @Theo @Samir @Jules

Theo (Solutions): Quick summary: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is preferred from a security posture because it avoids public ELBs in their VPC. Caveat: our backend still egresses from Redwood-managed IPs. If ShadowGates DPI terminates TLS, cert-based auth or mTLS can break. Two recommended patterns:
- PrivateLink only: simplest. Customer keeps TLS passthrough (no inspect) so end-to-end certs/mTLS remain intact.
- Connector-in-VPC: deploy a small connector (container/VM) in their subnet that forwards to Redwood. DPI can run locally and see plaintext; preserves client IPs and audit logs.

Samir (NetOps): Pasteable firewall snippet (minimal and copy-ready):
```
# ShadowGate POC - Redwood allowlist (example)
# replace <REDFW_EGRESS> and <PRIVLINK_ENI_CIDR> with values provided by Redwood

# Allow traffic from app subnets to PrivateLink ENIs
ALLOW tcp from <app_subnets> to <PRIVLINK_ENI_CIDR> port 443

# Allow outbound from connector/ENIs to Redwood egress IP(s)
ALLOW tcp from <connector_or_enis> to <REDFW_EGRESS> ports 443

# DNS / NTP
ALLOW udp from <connector_or_enis> to 8.8.8.8 port 53
ALLOW udp from <connector_or_enis> to <NTP_POOL> port 123
```

Samir (NetOps): Static egress option: we can provide a single /32 for the POC. For production we recommend an HA pair. Connector preserves client-srcip; PrivateLink alone will not preserve original client IP in Redwood logs.

Jules (Security): One-paragraph blurb for the packet (pasteable):
"Redwood will deploy an interface endpoint (PrivateLink) into ShadowGate-managed subnets for the POC. Outbound model requests initiated from the endpoint will egress from Redwood-managed static IP(s) provided to ShadowGate for allowlisting. If ShadowGates perimeter DPI terminates TLS, mutual authentication and certificate-based authorization may be impacted; in that case Redwood recommends deploying a lightweight connector inside the customer VPC so inspection occurs prior to egress and audit logs/client IPs remain preserved."

Jules (Security): Add bullets for questionnaire: TLS 1.2+ enforced; mTLS available for connector deployments. Data retention default is minimal; logs/export options can be contractually set.

Theo (Solutions): Pricing sketches to include in POC packet (estimates): static egress IP add-on (POC, pro-rated) = $1,600/month per IP; connector VM = ~$550/month + $1,200 one-time setup; Dedicated reserved capacity for sustained throughput or many IPs = starts ~$22k/month (size-dependent). Will confirm formal quote.

Marta (AE): Action items: Theo to confirm actual IP(s) and a firm quote by EOD Tue, Samir to attach a one-page network diagram and minimal subnet sizing by Mon, Jules to drop the paragraph + bullets into the security packet. bot-deploy: Created ticket POC-555: ShadowGate - PrivateLink DPI & egress.

Theo (Solutions): Acknowledged ":thumbsup:"

Samir (NetOps): Acknowledged - will share diagram Mon morning.

Jules (Security): Acknowledged - will add to packet and flag any legal consent language if inspection implies cert re-issuance.
